# Source and scope instructions

Read the complete indexed transcript. Canonical caption event indices are zero-based; timestamps and caption text must remain unchanged. This recording is Michael Shermer and Glen Scrivener debating “Can we be good without God?”, moderated by Vince Vitale. It was originally published by Premier Unbelievable in 2024 and reuploaded by Glen Scrivener in 2025.

## Explicitly approved scope

The user specifically authorized scoring only Shermer and Scrivener, using Vitale’s questions as context and evaluating their replies, with a clear disclosure. This is not the automatic 5% host-exclusion exception. Vitale is not a scored participant or teammate. His arguments cannot be credited to Scrivener, and neither primary speaker inherits his premises merely by answering. Primary speakers’ own arguments, adoption, qualifications and answers remain eligible. Consider opportunities fairly: Shermer receives multiple follow-up challenges; Scrivener must not receive credit for Vitale’s challenges or be penalized for lacking answers to questions never put to him.

Pro is Michael Shermer (“Morality without God”); con is Glen Scrivener (“Christian foundations of morality”). Both allow atheists to behave morally. The live disagreement concerns grounding, universal human worth and the historical/continuing role of Christianity. At about 52 minutes Scrivener allows objective or prosocial morality without Jesus but questions its kind and scope. Preserve that concession rather than inventing an absolute denial of every non-Christian moral truth. Distinguish historical origins from present philosophical justification, and distinguish grounds, knowledge and motivation. These are source distinctions, not directions to prefer a side or prescribe any rating.

The assessed window is 02:10.720 through the end of the last primary caption at 1:20:17.440. Read introductions and outro as attribution context, but opening promotion and closing host thanks are not scored. Complete discussion, concessions and closings must be reviewed; no isolated highlight sample.

English automatically generated captions are complete but not verbatim audio verification. Do not silently repair their words, names, numbers, citations or negation. Shermer, Scrivener and Vitale are frequently misrecognized; so are Nietzsche, Dostoevsky and other names. Choose exact quotations without corrupted terms.
